items.q: Elderly patient reading better without glasses (second sight) with browning lens has which cataract?
items.exp: Nuclear compaction raises refractive index shorting focus; transient near gain precedes dense brunescent blindness needing phaco. Cortical disease instead glares with spokes.
items.kp: New near vision in old brown lens: nuclear shift.

items.q: Diabetic on steroids with central glare worse in bright light most likely has which cataract?
items.exp: Plaque at the nodal point scatters oncoming light; early surgery restores before density plus diabetes complicates macula. Steroid and radiation histories match.
r: Incorrect. Peripheral spokes spare centre early.
items.kp: Bright light glare in steroid diabetic: posterior plaque.

items.q: Milky white lens with sinking brown nucleus inferiorly in neglected elderly eye is what and risk?
o: Morgagnian hypermature with phacolytic glaucoma risk
items.exp: Liquefied cortex leaks protein clogging trabeculum (phacolytic) while intact capsule mimics safety; urgent lens extraction with pressure control saves. Intumescent variants instead push iris closing angle.
items.kp: Milky lens, sunken nucleus: Morgagnian leaks pressure.

items.q: Newborn with bilateral dense white cataracts should be operated when and followed by what?
o: Within weeks (lensectomy vitrectomy infants) then aggressive amblyopia patching and refraction
items.exp: Visual deprivation amblyopia fixes within weeks; delayed surgery leaves permanent nystagmus and poor acuity despite clear media. Unilateral disease hurries even faster with contact lens rehabilitation.
items.kp: White pupils at birth: clear within weeks, patch for years.

items.q: Salt and pepper retinopathy with cataract and deafness in a newborn points to which cause?
items.exp: First trimester rubella scars lens, retina and cochlea with heart defects; MMR elimination campaigns prevent while galactosaemia instead oil drops reversibly with diet.
items.kp: Cataract plus deafness plus retinopathy: rubella.

items.q: Oil drop cataract in an infant that reverses with diet restriction is characteristic of what?
items.exp: Dulcitol accumulation swells fibres reversibly early; lactose free diet clears lens while delay mental retards. Cataract plus developmental delay screens metabolism.
items.kp: Sweet urine plus reversible cataract: galactose.

items.q: Blur months after excellent cataract surgery with pearls behind the lens is what and treated how?
items.exp: Migrating equatorial cells pearl the posterior capsule (Elschnig) or fibrose it; laser opens a clear window in minutes without re entering the eye. Detachment instead flashes with curtain.
r: Incorrect. No flashes or field cut.
items.kp: Good surgery gone hazy months later: YAG the capsule.

items.q: Swollen white lens with shallow chamber and acute high pressure in neglected cataract is which emergency?
o: Phacomorphic angle closure needing lens extraction with pressure control
items.exp: Intumescent lens pushes iris forward closing trabeculum; mannitol and acetazolamide bridge to urgent extraction while laser iridotomy alone fails against lens bulk.
items.kp: Fat lens shutting drain: extract the lens.

items.q: IOL power calculation chiefly needs which two measurements?
items.exp: Biometry predicts effective lens position and vergence; errors surprise refraction postoperatively needing exchange or piggyback lenses. Toric planning adds axis mapping.
items.kp: Measure eye length and curve to pick lens.

items.q: Cystoid macular oedema after complicated cataract surgery (Irvine Gass) presents how and treated?
o: Delayed central blur with petaloid leakage on OCT or angiography; topical NSAIDs with steroids
items.exp: Inflammatory mediators cyst the macula weeks postoperatively, especially with vitreous loss; NSAIDs with steroids resolve most while chronic cases need periocular or anti VEGF escalation.
items.kp: Post cataract central blur weeks later: macular cysts.
